verdicts.argument: Wording drift verified on both pages: FY2025 10-K p27 'has negatively affected our revenues and profit margins' vs FY2024 10-K p27 'could have an adverse effect'; I scanned every 340B sentence in both 10-Ks and the realized-tense sentence is new in FY2025. GTN table on BMY:10k_FY2025.md p49 verified: charge-backs and cash discounts 14,067 vs 11,510 (+22%), gross 88,085 vs 83,671 (+5%). Arithmetic checks: 13.76% x 88,085 = 12,117, excess about $1.95B; x0.812/2,039 = $0.78. The reader labels this an upper bound in the math, the estimate ('Up to') and the confidence reason, so it is not passed off as an estimate. Two materiality cautions: (1) p83 (Note 2) and p65 say charge-backs cover DoD/VA, 340B covered entities and cash discounts, and cash discounts scale with gross sales, so the 340B piece is unsized; (2) the same dollars are also claimed by c02. Of the ~$2.49B total GTN-rate excess in 2025 (41,329 vs 88,085 x 44.09% = 38,837), charge-backs are $1.95B, Medicaid/Medicare rebates only $0.59B, other -$0.05B. c01 and c02 cannot be added.
verdicts.correction: State it as: charge-backs explain about $1.95B (78%) of the ~$2.5B rise in BMS's 2025 GTN rate; 340B is one unsized component of that line alongside DoD/VA and cash discounts. Do not add this to c02's $2.9B, because they overlap.

verdicts.argument: Quotes and speaker verified: BMY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p1 is grade B, and the speakers are Adam Lenkowsky and Luisa Hector. In context, though, Lenkowsky's 'roughly equal' answers a question about Part D sales phasing. He says Eliquis sales are 'more even' through the year, offset by catastrophic-phase effects on Revlimid, Pomalyst and Camzyos. The filings (10-Q 2025Q3 p36; 10-K FY2025 p49) talk about the U.S. GTN rate. Those are different metrics, so this is not a like-for-like contradiction. The sizing also fails. The ~$2.9B (4 points x $71.7B U.S. gross) is a gross-deduction number, not a net revenue headwind, because the redesign also raises volume. The candidate text says $2.7B while the math says $2.9B, and the 49% and 53% are rounded (my back-solve from p83 and p49 gives ~3.8 points, about $2.7B). Worst of all, the 10-K line items do not let Part D be the 'primary' part of $2.9B. On p49, Medicaid and Medicare rebates (where Part D manufacturer discounts would land) were only ~$0.59B above the 2024 rate on 2025 gross; charge-backs were $1.95B. The 10-K driver sentence also names 'higher government channel mix' jointly with Part D. So the $1.15 EPS 'attributed mostly to Part D' is not supported, and it double-counts c01.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: the filings name Part D redesign plus government channel mix for a ~4-point U.S. GTN rise (~$2.7-2.9B of extra U.S. deductions, all of which were offset by $4.4B of gross growth). The Medicare/Medicaid rebate line contributed only ~$0.6B of the excess, so any Part D-specific sizing is at most about $0.6B unless BMS books Part D discounts elsewhere. The call remark was about sales phasing, not the GTN rate.

verdicts.argument: Amounts and dates verified. On BMY:10k_FY2025.md p34, Keytruda and Tecentriq royalties end 2026-12-31 and the diabetes royalty ended 2025-12-31; pretax royalties are ~$2.7B. p91: diabetes royalty income 1,121, Keytruda 588, Tecentriq 47 (sum 1,756). p91 also says Merck pays 2.5% through 2026-12-31 and Roche pays through 2026-12-31. BMY:10q_2026Q2.md p10: H1 2026 Keytruda 308, Tecentriq 26 (334); diabetes zero in 2026 (p10 and p38). MRK:10q_2026Q2.md p34 says 'will continue through 2026, terminating thereafter'. The math is right: 668 x 0.812 / 2,039 = $0.266, which is 3.9% of the $6.875 midpoint, and the non-GAAP tax guide is ~18% (release p6), close to the 18.8% used. The diabetes royalty did flow through non-GAAP EPS: 10-Q p28 cites its expiry as an offset in the non-GAAP EPS bridge, so the ~$0.45 2026 hit is in the right metric. Small issues: (1) H1 x2 likely understates because Keytruda grows (Q2 149 vs Q1 159 is flat, so close enough); (2) the 2025 18.8% rate is inflated by the non-deductible Orbital charge (p58); (3) the hit lands in 2027 and should be compared with 2027 EPS, not the 2026 guide; (4) the Winrevair 'offset' is booked in Other revenues (p92), not OI&E, so it is a separate, already-growing stream, not a replacement. The diabetes piece is a past event that was already absorbed in 2026 and reported in the 10-Q.
verdicts.correction: Lead with the 2027 piece only: about $0.62-0.67B pretax, roughly $0.26-0.27 of EPS (~4%), from the Keytruda and Tecentriq royalties ending on 2026-12-31. Present the $1.76B total as history, since $1.12B of it is already gone and visible in 2026 results.

verdicts.argument: Numbers verified on BMY:10q_2026Q2.md p31. The 52% and 34% are the same ratio (U.S. GTN adjustments / U.S. gross product sales) on the same-quarter base, so the definitions match. But the denominator is the thing the list cut shrank: gross fell $4,002M while net product sales rose only $679M company-wide. The rate drop is mostly mechanical and says little about how much net price rose. The core math error: a $2,757M drop in a deduction line is presented as the upside, but it is offset by the $4.0B gross decline. Eliquis net revenue rose only $801M year over year in Q2 (4,481 vs 3,680, p8), and that already includes demand and FX. The GTN table is also company-wide, not Eliquis-only. The attribution '~$1.4B of 2026 Eliquis upside is a rebate-formula effect, not demand' is contradicted by the company's own pages: 10-Q p35 says Eliquis grew 'primarily due to higher demand, foreign exchange impacts ... and higher average net selling prices in the U.S.' (demand listed first); release p2 says 'Demand increased for Eliquis'; release p6 attributes the total-revenue raise to 'broad-based and continuing momentum across the portfolio'. The $1.44B is just 10 points x $14,443M, the size of the guidance raise, with no split. Reserve releases ($485M vs $159M, 10-K p49) are real, but releases recur every year ($331M in H1 2025, $67M in H1 2026), so calling 2025 'flattered' by ~$0.13 EPS overstates the one-off share. The $485M is 1.0% of revenue.
verdicts.correction: Say: the 2026 U.S. Eliquis list cut lowered gross sales and rebates together, and the U.S. GTN rate fell from 52% to 34%. The net price benefit is not disclosed; it sits within the $801M (+22%) Q2 Eliquis increase, which the 10-Q attributes to demand, FX and higher U.S. net price. Do not claim $1.44B of rebate effect or that this is 'not demand'.

verdicts.argument: Arithmetic verified on BMY:10k_FY2025.md p107-108: gross trade receivables +14.2%, charge-back reserve +91% (1,720 vs 900), net +6.4%, inventory +5.2%, WIP +23.9%. Revenue: FY -0.2% (p48), Q4 +1.3% (Q4 release p2). DSO is 70.6 vs 67.2 days. The candidate itself concludes there is no channel stuffing. The only signal is the $820M reserve build, which is a balance-sheet presentation of the same charge-back GTN already counted in c01 and has no separate P&L effect. Net DSO rose 3 days, worth ~$0.4B of one-time working capital on a $48B revenue base, and the receivable reversed to 9,962 by Q2 2026 (10-Q p18). It is below materiality and duplicates c01; the 'price protection ahead of the list cut' explanation is undisclosed speculation.
verdicts.correction: Fold into c01 as a supporting data point (the charge-back reserve nearly doubled at year-end 2025). It is not a standalone finding.

verdicts.argument: Facts verified. Abecma was 427 in 2025 (10-K p85), and footnote (a) added Abecma in 10-Q 2026Q1 p8. Restated Q2 2025 'Other Growth' 557 = 470 + Abecma 87 (10-Q 2025Q2 p8). Q2 2026 bucket is 653 (+17%). Winrevair 289 vs 107 (10-K p92). But Abecma is 0.9% of revenue, below the 1% bar, and the 'hidden' decline is about $60M a year (0.12% of revenue, ~$0.02 EPS before costs). The reader concedes it is 'small in dollars'. A disclosure-visibility point with no material number does not move an investor's view.
verdicts.correction: Keep only as a one-line footnote on disclosure practice; it is immaterial on revenue and EPS.

verdicts.argument: CMS fact sheet p2 verified: Eliquis MFP $231 vs 2023 list $521; Xarelto $197 vs $517. The 1.36x and 2.83x are not on any page. They come from fact rows pricing/gtn_proxy.csv#40 and #155 (verify_status 'verified', but computed by the pipeline from nadac_history.csv, whose raw nadac rows are unverified_raw machine data under HELPERS.md). They can be cited as derived fact rows but cannot be quoted as a source, and the raw NADAC must not be deep-linked. Row #155 notes that Xarelto NADAC 'mixes EA/ML NDCs; collector simple mean is not a valid per-unit price'; its MFP unit range is 1.329-6.881, so the 2.83x relies on the EA-only weighted subset. On materiality, '44% cheaper at the pharmacy in every non-Medicare channel' compares acquisition-cost (list proxy) prices. Medicaid gets Eliquis free, and commercial net prices are after confidential rebates, so this is not a net-price gap in any channel except cash-pay or coinsurance. The $714M U.S. Q2 increase (3,357/1.27) checks, but the 10-Q p35 assigns it to demand, FX and net price, not to a price gap against Xarelto. J&J's 10-Q p40 says Xarelto sales increased (patient mix), with 'continued share erosion'.
verdicts.correction: Say: after the 2026 list cut, Eliquis's pharmacy acquisition cost (NADAC, derived fact row) is ~1.36x its MFP vs ~2.83x for Xarelto (EA NDCs only). This is a list-level gap, not a net-price gap, and the share effect is not sized. Cite as fact rows, not quotes.

verdicts.argument: Label text verified: drug:eliquis:label_sections.md p39 (no dose adjustment incl. ESRD on dialysis) and drug:xarelto:label_sections.md p24 (avoid at CrCl <15 incl. dialysis), plus p7, p8 and p12. The CMS p2 ratios check: 3,928,000/1,324,000 = 2.97x enrollees and $18.3B/$6.3B = 2.90x spend. But the impact is explicitly 'not separately sized'. The ESRD/dialysis subgroup cannot plausibly explain a 2.6M-enrollee gap, so the causal 'helps explain' is unsupported by any number. 'IRA bites Eliquis harder than any other BMS product' is trivially true for 2026 and not a sized effect. The comparison of CMS Part D gross spend (2023-24 data) with 2025 BMS net sales mixes periods and gross vs net, which the reader flags.
verdicts.correction: Keep as a fine-print fact (the renal/dialysis label edge), with no revenue or causal claim attached.

verdicts.argument: Eliquis is material: $14,443M was 30% of 2025 revenue (Q4 release p6; 10-K p48), and Q2 2026 Eliquis is $4,481M of $12,973M (10-Q p8). Xarelto is a fair comparator with the same 2026 MFP year (CMS p2). The fine-print edge (the renal/dialysis label wording) is verified on the label pages, but it carries no dollar sizing.
verdicts.correction: Pick holds; present the label edge as qualitative.

overall: Every quote verifies on its page, and the royalty cliff (c03) is the one finding whose numbers, dates, metric (non-GAAP EPS) and counterparty confirmation all hold; the 340B drift (c01) holds as an explicitly labelled upper bound. The gross-to-net cluster (c02, c04, c07) repeatedly treats deduction-line swings as revenue impact, double-counts the same 2025 GTN excess (~$2.5B total, 78% charge-backs) across c01 and c02, and attributes the Eliquis 2026 raise to rebates when the 10-Q and release credit demand first.
